findings.title: Security header not observed: Content-Security-Policy
findings.description: The Content-Security-Policy header was not observed in the response from https://example.com/. A CSP can limit which sources a page may load scripts and other content from, which reduces the impact of cross-site scripting.
findings.remediation: Review whether a Content-Security-Policy suits this site, and consider starting in report-only mode.

findings.title: Security header not observed: Strict-Transport-Security
findings.description: The Strict-Transport-Security header was not observed in the response from https://example.com/. HSTS tells browsers to use HTTPS only, which protects against downgrade attempts.
findings.remediation: Consider adding Strict-Transport-Security with a suitable max-age once the whole site works over HTTPS.

findings.title: Security header not observed: X-Content-Type-Options
findings.description: The X-Content-Type-Options header was not observed in the response from https://example.com/. The nosniff value stops browsers from guessing content types, which can reduce some content-confusion issues.

findings.title: Security header not observed: X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors
findings.description: The X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors header was not observed in the response from https://example.com/. Without either, other sites may be able to embed this page in a frame, which can enable clickjacking.
findings.remediation: Consider adding a CSP frame-ancestors directive (or X-Frame-Options) that limits who can frame the site.

findings.title: Security header not observed: Referrer-Policy
findings.description: The Referrer-Policy header was not observed in the response from https://example.com/. Without a policy, browsers decide how much of the page URL is sent to other sites.
findings.remediation: Consider adding a Referrer-Policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

findings.title: Redirect from HTTP to HTTPS not observed
findings.description: A request to http://example.com/ was answered over plain HTTP and did not redirect to HTTPS. Visitors who use the http:// address may stay on an unencrypted connection.
findings.remediation: Consider redirecting all HTTP requests to HTTPS, and pair it with an HSTS header once the whole site works over HTTPS.

findings.title: CAA record not observed
findings.description: No CAA record was observed for example.com. CAA records restrict which certificate authorities may issue certificates for a domain.
findings.remediation: Consider adding a CAA record naming the certificate authorities you use.

findings.title: TCP port 80 observed open
findings.description: Port 80 on example.com accepted a TCP connection. This is normal for a web server.
findings.remediation: No action needed if this port is meant to be public.

findings.title: TCP port 443 observed open
findings.description: Port 443 on example.com accepted a TCP connection. This is normal for a web server.
findings.remediation: No action needed if this port is meant to be public.
